environment.name: BETTERMEMORY_DIR
environment.sets: the store directory (resolution rule 1, before [storage] directory, ./.claude-memory and the user default); the store file is <dir>/store/memory.sqlite

environment.name: BETTERMEMORY_KEYS_DIR
environment.sets: the key ring's directory (else the user config directory's keys)

environment.name: BETTERMEMORY_STATE_DIR
environment.sets: the daemon state directory: daemon-<digest>.json, its locks and log (else the user state directory)

environment.name: BETTERMEMORY_CLIENT
environment.sets: the client name a stdio server records as the caller

environment.name: BETTERMEMORY_CLIENT_VERSION
environment.sets: the client version recorded with it

environment.name: BETTERMEMORY_MODEL
environment.sets: the model name recorded with it

environment.name: BETTERMEMORY_WORKSPACE
environment.sets: the caller's workspace (before MCP roots and the cwd)

environment.name: CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID
environment.sets: Claude Code's session id: the hooks' session; removed from a daemon's environment

environment.name: CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED
environment.sets: Claude Code's attended flag; "1" when a person is at the session (the capture checkpoint asks only then); removed from a daemon's environment

environment.name: CLAUDE_CODE_CUSTOM_OAUTH_URL
environment.sets: when set, Claude Code's per-user files carry the -custom-oauth suffix

placeholders.<scratch>: the run's temporary directory (an absolute path); the path after it is written with / whatever the platform's separator

read: catalogue: every key the config file accepts, in the loader's order (section, key, type, default, managed_may_pin: a managed file's line for it is in force over the user's). fixed: the keys that are fixed values and no settings (config.FIXED_SETTINGS); limit names the write limits whose managed line was stricter. coercion: each kept key read alone from each value of probes (TOML values, in order): reads[i] is {value, warned} or {refused: the error text, warned}, the error locating the line in config.toml; warned says the loader logged a warning; check is [level, code] of each finding `config check` reports for a config.toml holding that one line (a finding can stand where nothing was logged, e.g. a float truncated to an integer). on_bad_value: refuse when a table stops the load, default when it reads as the default. environment: the variables read; config_path: `config path --json` with the location variables set. cases: config_toml / managed_toml (null: no file; *_hex: the bytes, when they are not UTF-8) -> check and show, each the exit code and the text the CLI printed (one JSON document, where a non-finite float prints bare as NaN or Infinity), or raised: the exception that escaped the command; each command runs with the loader's one-shot notices cleared, as a CLI process of its own would; and audit_config_findings, the config findings of `security audit` (posture._settings over the config the audit loads). Check exits 0 (nothing above a note), 1 (an error), 2 (warnings only). The cases whose text is the interpreter's are in settings_python.json; those that expand or resolve a path are in settings_paths.json and settings_paths_python.json.
setup: Every location variable points into <scratch> (_sandbox.world): BETTERMEMORY_DIR=<scratch>/mem, BETTERMEMORY_KEYS_DIR=<scratch>/keys, BETTERMEMORY_STATE_DIR=<scratch>/state, HOME=<scratch>/home. The user's config file is <scratch>/user/config.toml (config.default_config_path answers it) and the managed file <scratch>/managed/managed.toml (managed.managed_config_path answers it); a case that has no text for one has no such file. The CLI runs in process (cli.main with argv set).
